intended_object: For an object B of an abelian category and an object property P, a "P-admissible layer" of B is a pair of subobjects L ≤ U of B (an interval in the subobject lattice) whose subquotient U/L satisfies P. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The structure has two subobjects `lower` and `upper` of B with `lower ≤ upper`, and requires P to hold for `cokernel (Subobject.ofLE lower upper _)`. The map `ofLE` is the inclusion of L into U, viewed as subobjects, so its cokernel is the subquotient U/L. This matches the docstring ("nested pair of subobjects with an admissible chosen quotient") and the module documentation. P is not assumed closed under isomorphisms. That is harmless: the docstring says explicitly that admissibility is tested on the chosen quotient, and for the usual iso-closed properties this is the same as testing any representative of U/L. The notion is specific to this library and has no Mathlib counterpart. Mathlib's closest notions are subobject intervals and `Subobject.ofLE`, but nothing bundles a property of the subquotient. Working in an abelian category is the natural setting for subquotients and for the later results in the file, such as the embedding of U/(L ⊓ D) into U/L × B/D. The definition is not too narrow, and I found no correctness problems.
